sources.title: Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025
Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026

claims.text: RTX supplies commercial aerospace systems, aircraft engines and defense technologies. It combines aircraft production and aftermarket exposure with government procurement.

evidence.locator: Item 1, General; Business Segments

claims.text: The three segments are Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney and Raytheon. Revenue includes equipment sales, parts, repairs, engine support and defense contracts.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Business Segments

claims.text: Examples include Collins aircraft systems, Pratt & Whitney GTF and F135 engines, and Raytheon Patriot, AMRAAM and radar systems.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Business Segments / Collins Aerospace; Pratt & Whitney; Raytheon

claims.text: Customers include airframe manufacturers, aircraft operators, U.S. government agencies and international buyers. Commercial aviation and defense create distinct demand drivers.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Business Segments; Sales and Customers

claims.text: Original engine and aircraft-system placements create later service opportunities. Supplier reliability, overhaul capacity and regulatory approval affect delivery and service economics.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Competition; Item 1A, suppliers and product quality

claims.text: The filing describes competition in aircraft equipment, spares and defense systems. Defense suppliers may also be partners or competitors on different programs.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Competition

claims.text: Interpretation: installed engines and certified systems can support aftermarket durability. Alternative parts suppliers, pricing competition and maintenance obligations limit the advantage.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Competition; Item 1A, product performance

claims.text: Backlog increased from USD 289 billion at June 30, 2026 to USD 340 billion at September 30, 2026. Commercial backlog moved from USD 170 billion to USD 176 billion and defense from USD 119 billion to USD 164 billion. Third-quarter awards included multiyear Tomahawk and AMRAAM production contracts whose terms were not yet fully definitized.

evidence.locator: Second quarter 2026 highlights / backlog, line 39
Third quarter 2026 highlights / backlog and undefinitized production contracts, lines 39–40

claims.text: In the third quarter of 2026, Collins commercial aftermarket sales grew 9% year over year, Pratt & Whitney commercial aftermarket sales grew 21%, and Raytheon total sales grew 14%.

evidence.locator: Segment Results / Collins, Pratt & Whitney and Raytheon growth commentary, lines 123–125, 159–162 and 195

claims.text: The July results reported commercial aftermarket and defense growth. Management plans capacity and productivity improvements; future backlog conversion still depends on execution.

evidence.locator: Opening management commentary; Segment Results
Opening management commentary, lines 47–48; Segment Results

claims.text: For July 1–September 30, 2026, GAAP sales were USD 24,965 million versus USD 22,478 million in the comparable 2025 quarter. Net income attributable to common shareowners was USD 2,583 million and diluted EPS was USD 1.89.

evidence.locator: Condensed Consolidated Statement of Operations / quarter ended September 30, 2026 and 2025; lines 236–333

claims.text: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, company-defined non-GAAP adjusted diluted EPS was USD 2.26 versus USD 1.70 a year earlier. The adjusted figure includes USD 0.25 of IEEPA cost recovery; the recovery was not removed by the non-GAAP reconciliation.

evidence.locator: Third quarter 2026 highlights / IEEPA recovery, lines 34–52; Adjusted Income, Earnings Per Share, and Effective Tax Rate / diluted EPS, lines 1066–1077

claims.text: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, GAAP operating cash flow was USD 2,868 million, including approximately USD 300 million of IEEPA recovery; capital expenditures were USD 749 million and non-GAAP free cash flow was USD 2,119 million. The comparable 2025 values were USD 4,639 million, USD 614 million and USD 4,025 million, respectively. Nine-month free cash flow was USD 6,306 million versus USD 4,745 million. Free cash flow equals operating cash flow less capital expenditures.

evidence.locator: Third quarter 2026 / cash flow commentary, lines 38 and 52; Free Cash Flow Reconciliation, lines 1198–1221

claims.text: Pratt & Whitney reported operating profit of USD 608 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 versus USD 751 million a year earlier. Its non-GAAP adjusted operating profit was USD 968 million: a USD 363 million customer-bankruptcy charge was excluded, while approximately USD 160 million of IEEPA recovery remained in adjusted profit.

evidence.locator: Pratt & Whitney segment results, lines 137–162; adjusted operating profit reconciliation, lines 824–839

claims.text: For April 1–June 30, 2026, GAAP sales were USD 24,708 million, net income attributable to common shareowners USD 2,139 million and diluted EPS USD 1.57.

evidence.locator: Condensed Consolidated Statement of Operations
Condensed Consolidated Statement of Operations / quarter ended June 30, 2026, lines 234–330

claims.text: Adjusted diluted EPS was USD 1.89 for that quarter. This company-defined non-GAAP measure excludes acquisition accounting and specified restructuring and other items.

evidence.locator: Summary Financial Results; EPS reconciliation
Summary Financial Results and adjusted EPS reconciliation, lines 72–81 and 1042–1053

claims.text: At September 30, 2026, GAAP cash and equivalents were USD 9,173 million. Long-term debt was USD 31,490 million excluding current maturities of USD 5,679 million; separate short-term borrowings were USD 210 million. Operating lease liabilities are not included in these debt figures.

evidence.locator: Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet / cash, short-term borrowings, long-term debt and current maturities, lines 508–564

claims.text: At June 30, 2026, GAAP cash and equivalents were USD 8,305 million. GAAP long-term debt was USD 31,858 million, excluding current maturities of USD 5,296 million and separate short-term borrowings of USD 229 million.

evidence.locator: Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet
Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet / June 30, 2026, lines 496–552

claims.text: The July results identify Chris Calio as chairman and CEO. The September succession filing names Jill Albertelli as Pratt & Whitney’s future president.

evidence.locator: Opening management commentary
Item 5.02, Retirement of Named Executive Officer

claims.text: Interpretation: value recurring segment profit and cash generation after separating cost recoveries, customer-credit charges and acquisition adjustments. The larger backlog does not establish delivery timing or profit. No current stock price, valuation multiple or price target is supplied.

evidence.locator: Third quarter 2026 / IEEPA recovery; Pratt & Whitney results; Use and Definitions of Non-GAAP Financial Measures; Free Cash Flow Reconciliation

claims.text: Announced September 15, 2026: Jill Albertelli is scheduled to succeed Shane Eddy as Pratt & Whitney president on January 1, 2027. Execution effects remain uncertain.

evidence.locator: Item 5.02, Retirement of Named Executive Officer

claims.text: Powder-metal issues require accelerated GTF inspections and additional shop visits. Costs depend on inspection findings, overhaul capacity and customer compensation; deteriorating estimates would weaken a cash-recovery thesis.

evidence.locator: Note 16, Pratt & Whitney Powder Metal Matter

claims.text: Interpretation: raised cash guidance and a larger defense backlog strengthen the execution case, but the quarterly cash decline, recovery-assisted earnings and customer-credit charge limit confidence in recurring profit. A miss of the new cash-flow floor, repeat customer-credit losses or sustained defense sales contraction would weaken this thesis. These are analyst monitoring conditions, not company forecasts.

evidence.locator: Full-year outlook; Summary Financial Results; Pratt & Whitney results; Raytheon results

claims.text: Interpretation: upside combines aftermarket growth with profitable defense deliveries; downside includes engine remediation, supply constraints or contract overruns. No scenario probabilities or target prices are assigned.

evidence.locator: Item 2, Business Overview; Note 16, Commitments and Contingencies

claims.text: Review scope: the current earnings comparison uses the complete issuer results releases. Changes in detailed engine-remediation cash obligations, customer-credit exposure and litigation remain unverified because the new SEC quarterly filing and current report, call transcript and presentation were not reviewed. Earlier filing-based risks retain their original evidence dates.

evidence.locator: Issuer release / financial statements, reconciliations and Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements
Preceding issuer release / financial statements and full-year outlook

claims.text: Pratt & Whitney’s F135 powers Lockheed Martin’s F-35. This is a documented propulsion-platform relationship; shared defense exposure alone does not establish another customer relationship.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Pratt & Whitney / F135

claims.text: On October 20, 2026, RTX raised full-year 2026 non-GAAP guidance from the July outlook: adjusted sales USD 95.0–96.0 billion to USD 97.0–97.5 billion; organic sales growth 8–9% to 10–11%; adjusted EPS USD 7.10–7.25 to USD 7.65–7.75; and free cash flow USD 8.50–8.75 billion to USD 9.0–9.2 billion. These ranges are forecasts.

evidence.locator: Updates outlook for full year 2026, lines 41–46
Updates outlook for full year 2026, lines 41–46

claims.text: RTX raised its adjusted sales, adjusted EPS and free-cash-flow outlook on July 23, 2026. These were management forecasts, not realized annual results.

evidence.locator: Updates outlook for full year 2026
Updates outlook for full year 2026, lines 41–46

gaps: No current stock price, consensus estimates or valuation multiples were sourced.

Quarterly results through September 30, 2026 were reviewed in the full issuer release published October 20, 2026. The new SEC quarterly filing and current report were not accessed; their notes, exhibits and disclosure completeness remain unreviewed.
No earnings-call transcript or presentation was reviewed; engine-remediation cash schedules, aircraft-on-ground trends, debt maturities and litigation changes still need filing-level verification.
Named commercial aerospace competitors and market shares require separate primary-source comparison.
Earlier annual-business and succession evidence retains its original source access dates; this is a bounded earnings update, not an exhaustive news or contract-award refresh.
